# Malaria Deaths Rise to 610,000 in 2024

An estimated 610,000 people died from malaria in 2024, according to the latest [figures](https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/reports/world-malaria-report-2025/) by the World Health Organization (WHO).

The toll is far below the 864,000 deaths recorded in 2000, reflecting years of strong political commitment and global investment, which expanded access to insecticide-treated bed nets (ITNs), rapid diagnostic tests and artemisinin-based combination therapies.
However, progress has stalled in recent years.

Between 2019 and 2020, malaria deaths surged by about 54,000 worldwide, as the [Covid-19 pandemic](https://www.statista.com/topics/5994/the-coronavirus-disease-covid-19-outbreak/) disrupted prevention, diagnosis and treatment.

Although this was followed by a partial recovery, with deaths declining from 621,000 in 2020 to 598,000 in 2023, the latest available data shows how there has been an increase again, this time by 12,000 deaths between 2023 and 2024.

Africa remains the epicenter of the crisis, accounting for roughly 95 percent of global deaths, with Madagascar (+4,900), Ethiopia (+3,800) and Yemen (+932) together accounting for 85 percent of the increase.
Sudan accounted for more than half of these (57.5 percent).

Although the region saw a decline of 700 deaths compared with 2023, this was largely driven by a significant reduction in Pakistan (-2,000 estimated deaths), while Yemen (+932), Sudan (+189), Afghanistan (+68) and Somalia (+37) all reported increases.

South-East Asia has made major progress in the fight against [malaria](https://www.statista.com/topics/3065/malaria/?srsltid=AfmBOoo1Evi7ZdwZPt0eJ5La7B4W59GurJ1FKQEi1n15_TR6N4Z4-DON), reducing annual malaria deaths from 36,500 in 2000 to 3,900 in 2024, a drop of 89 percent.
After more than halving between 2000 and 2015, malaria deaths rose by 29.2 percent between 2015 and 2024.
An estimated 504 people died there in 2024, with Haiti experiencing a nearly fourfold increase in deaths between 2023 and 2024.
Meanwhile, the WHO European Region has remained malaria-free since 2015.
The situation worsened in 2025 amid sharp cuts to foreign aid, exacerbating longstanding underinvestment in healthcare systems across many affected countries.

According to the latest World malaria report, there were 282 million cases of malaria in 2024, an increase of about 9 million cases (3%) compared with 2023.
The estimated number of malaria deaths stood at 610 000 in 2024 compared to 598 000 in 2023.
The WHO African Region continues to carry a disproportionately high share of the global malaria burden.
In 2024 the Region was home to about 95% of all malaria cases and deaths.
Children under 5 years of age accounted for about 76% of all malaria deaths in the Region.
### Vaccine
Since October 2021, WHO has recommended broad use of the RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine among children living in regions with moderate to high *P. falciparum* malaria transmission.
The vaccine has been shown to significantly reduce malaria, and deadly severe malaria, among young children.
In October 2023, WHO recommended a second safe and effective malaria vaccine, R21/Matrix-M.
## Treatment
Most medicines used are in pill form.
Some people may need to go to a health centre or hospital for injectable medicines.
### Antimalarial drug resistance
## Genetic mutations
In 2024, these mutated parasites were reported in 42 malaria endemic countries; with Viet Nam reporting for the first time in 2024.
Although the estimated prevalence is still low in most countries, it exceeds 15% in Brazil, Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Nicaragua and Peru.
## Elimination
Continued measures to prevent re-establishment of transmission are required.
In 2024, 37 countries reported fewer than 1000 indigenous cases of the disease, up from just 13 countries in 2000.

Countries that have achieved at least 3 consecutive years of zero indigenous cases of malaria are eligible to apply for the [WHO certification of malaria elimination](/teams/global-malaria-programme/elimination/certification-process).

Since 2017, 14 countries have been certified by the WHO Director-General as malaria-free, including Maldives (2015), Sri Lanka (2016), Kyrgyzstan (2016), Paraguay (2018), Uzbekistan (2018), Argentina (2019), Algeria (2019), China (2021), El Salvador (2021), Azerbaijan (2023), Tajikistan (2023), Belize (2023), Cabo Verde (2024), Egypt (2024), Georgia (2025), Suriname (2025) and Timor-Leste (2025).

passages: Malaria facts & statistics 2025

The World Health Organization's[2025 World malaria report](https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/reports/world-malaria-report-2025) assesses global and regional malaria trends, highlights progress towards global targets and describes opportunities and challenges in controlling and eliminating the disease.
This year’s edition, 'Addressing the threat of antimalarial drug resistance', highlights that although there has been notable progress against the disease, it is not being made fast enough.
Malaria continues to disproportionately affect women and children living in poverty, which in turn fuels existing inequities.

In 2024, available malaria funding of US$ 3.9 billion fell far short of the Global Technical Strategy (GTS) target of US$ 9.3 billion by 2025. [MMV echoes the call for stronger investments in innovation and health systems](https://www.mmv.org/newsroom/news-resources-search/who-launches-2025-world-malaria-report-pressure-drug-resistance).
Below are some highlights from the 2025 report.
![2025 Global trends in malaria case incidence and mortality rate](/sites/default/files/styles/landscape_16_9_xsmall/public/content/image/Global%20cases%20and%20deaths.png.jpeg?itok=DAuJQU47)
WHO World Malaria Report 2025
Malaria remains a serious global health challenge, particularly in the hard-hit African Region.
* An estimated 282 million new malaria cases in 80 endemic countries worldwide in 2024, up from 273 million in 2023.
* Three countries – Ethiopia, Madagascar and Yemen – accounted for 58% of the estimated case increase from 2023 to 2024.
* Ten countries account for 66% of all malaria cases worldwide: Nigeria, DRC, Uganda, Ethiopia, Mozambique, Angola, Tanzania, Cote d’Ivoire, Mali and Burkina Faso.
* Total malaria deaths increased, with 610,000 malaria deaths in 2024 vs. 598,000 deaths reported in 2023.
* The WHO Africa Region accounts for 94% of cases and 95% of deaths globally.
* In Africa, 75% of malaria deaths were in children under 5 years old.
* Elimination is now within reach in three countries in the Greater Mekong subregion (GMS): Cambodia, the Lao People’s Democratic Republic and Vietnam.
![World Malaria report 2025](/sites/default/files/styles/landscape_16_9_xsmall/public/content/image/casesdeath%20averted.png.jpeg?itok=xYBZf9Qt)
WHO World malaria report 2025
Malaria responses worldwide are preventing illness and saving lives:
* Globally, an estimated 2.3 billion malaria cases and 14 million malaria deaths have been averted since 2000.

* [**Seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC)**](https://www.mmv.org/our-work/access-medicines/seasonal-malaria-chemoprevention)continues to scale up, reaching an average of 55 million children in 2025 at high risk of severe malaria in 19 countries.
* **Perennial malaria chemoprevention (PMC)** was implemented in at least 8 countries with nearly 1 million children aged under 24 months receiving their first dose of PMC in 2024.
* **Two vaccines are being rolled out**, with a total of 24 countries having introduced them by October 2025 through routine childhood immunization care.

* **Insecticide-treated net (ITN)** use remains generally unchanged, with almost half (47%) of those at risk of malaria sleeping under them. However, significant progress has been made to distribute nets that are more effective at combatting insecticide resistance.
* **Intermittent Preventive Treatment in pregnancy (IPTp)** was stable in 2024 (45% vs. 43% in 2023), which still falls short of the global target of 80%.

## Spotlight on MMV's work on equitable access
### Beyond ACTs
![Use of ACT in children](/sites/default/files/styles/landscape_16_9_xsmall/public/content/image/Use%20of%20ACTs%20in%20children.png.jpeg?itok=OZlSSul0)
WHO world malaria report 2025

In 2025, MMV and Novartis announced that [Coartem Baby became the first malaria medicine to be authorized for young infants](https://www.mmv.org/newsroom/news-resources-search/coartemr-baby-launches-ghana).
![54 million children received SMC in 2024 (partial data)](/sites/default/files/styles/landscape_16_9_xsmall/public/content/image/SMC_54million.png.jpeg?itok=47dXtQoA)
An average 54 million children received SMC across 19 countries in 2024 (partial data).
* SMC, an MMV-supported intervention, reached on average 56 million children in 19 African countries in 2025.
* Nigeria, which carries the highest malaria burden of any country, accounted for over half of the children who received SMC.
* The number of children receiving a fifth cycle of SMC is gradually increasing.
![IPTp scale up](/sites/default/files/styles/landscape_16_9_xsmall/public/content/image/IPTp%20scale%20up.png.jpeg?itok=sPfVb95z)
WHO World malaria report 2025

MMV has worked with pharmaceutical manufacturers in Kenya and Nigeria to support them in achieving quality assurance from WHO for the preventive medicines used for SMC and IPTp, which helps ensure medicines are manufactured where they are needed most.

In 2024, Swiss Pharma Nigeria Limited (Swipha), with support from MMV and Unitaid, became the [first Nigerian manufacturer of WHO-prequalified sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine](https://www.mmv.org/newsroom/news-resources-search/first-nigerian-manufacturer-obtains-who-prequalification-key-malaria), used for preventing malaria in children and pregnant women. # Malaria
Malaria transmission occurs in 80 countries across five WHO regions.
Since 2015, the WHO European Region has been free of malaria.
According to the
, there were 282 million estimated cases of malaria globally in 2024, with an incidence of 64 cases per 1000 population at risk.
This is an increase of 9 million cases from the previous year and a rise in incidence from 62.7 cases per 1000 population at risk in 2023.
Globally, in 2024, the number of deaths was estimated at 610 000, with a mortality rate of 13.8 per 100 000 population at risk.

The WHO African Region continues to carry the heaviest burden of malaria, accounting for an estimated 94% of malaria cases and 95% of malaria deaths worldwide in 2024; 75% of all deaths in this region were among children aged under 5 years old.
Source: WMR2025
## Related topics
### Countries with indigenous cases in 2000 and their status by 2024
Countries and areas with zero indigenous cases for at least 3 consecutive years are considered to have eliminated malaria.
In 2024, Bhutan reported zero indigenous cases for 3 consecutive years.

Malaysia reported zero indigenous cases caused by human *Plasmodium* species for the seventh consecutive year; Malaysia has a significant number of indigenous malaria cases caused by *Plasmodium knowlesi*infection.
Saudi Arabia reported zero indigenous cases for the fourth consecutive year.
Countries recently certified by the WHO Director-General as malaria-free, include: Cabo Verde (2024), Egypt (2024), Georgia (2025), Suriname (2025) and Timor-Leste (2025).
